See also: songé and Songe

English

[edit]

Noun

[edit]

songe (plural songes)

  1. Obsolete spelling of song.

Anagrams

[edit]
  • ENGOs, Genos, Goens, NGEOs, genos, geons, onegs, segno

French

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Old French songe, from Latin somnium. Compare Italian sogno, Spanish sueño and Portuguese sonho.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /sɔ̃ʒ/
  • Audio:(file)
  • Audio (France (Toulouse)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Brétigny-sur-Orge)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Vosges)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Massy)):(file)

Noun

[edit]

songe m (plural songes)

  1. (literary) dream
    Synonym: rêve
    • 1640, Pierre Corneille, Horace, act I, scene 2:
      C'est en contraire sens qu'un songe s'interprète.
      It is contrarily that one interprets a dream.

Related terms

[edit]
  • songer
  • songeur

Further reading

[edit]
  • “songe”, in Trésor de la langue française informatisé [Digitized Treasury of the French Language], 2012

Middle English

[edit]

Noun

[edit]

songe

  1. alternative form of song

Old English

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈson.ɡe/, [ˈsoŋ.ɡe]

Noun

[edit]

songe

  1. dative singular of song

Old French

[edit]

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • sonje

Etymology

[edit]

From Latin somnium.

Noun

[edit]

songe oblique singular, m (oblique plural songes, nominative singular songes, nominative plural songe)

  1. dream

Related terms

[edit]
  • songier

Descendants

[edit]
  • French: songe
  • Franc-Comtois: sondge
